explication: HAMi is Kubernetes GPU virtualization and heterogeneous accelerator scheduling middleware. A workload is submitted to the Kubernetes API, admitted and mutated by the webhook, filtered/scored/bound by the scheduler, then allocated by a device plugin during kubelet startup. The plugin selects physical or virtual devices, emits CDI/runtime configuration, and the workload runs under device-specific limits. Monitoring exports accelerator usage to Prometheus. The graph emphasizes documented workflow and sampled implementations; several vendor backends are represented by their shared device registry rather than unsampled internals.
